Serpentine is a board name, not a city neighbourhood.

The ground the label covers is Surrey's southern lowland: acreages and farm parcels along 40 Avenue, 176 Street (Highway 15), 168 Street, 184 Street, 188 Street and 196 Street, toward Morgan Creek, Campbell Heights and the South Surrey border country.
The name matches the land: Surrey's coastal floodplain stretches along the Nicomekl and Serpentine Rivers toward Cloverdale and Newton, and most of it is protected by river dykes along those rivers.
The stock here is acreage-led, not strata-led: estate houses on multi-acre parcels, working blueberry farms, and vacant land, rather than named condo or townhome complexes.

At the eastern edge, Campbell Heights adds industrial-side parcels: the South Campbell Heights Plan area alone is about 249 hectares centred on the Little Campbell River around 16 Avenue and 192 Street.
Farm parcels dominate the lowland: most of Surrey's Serpentine and Nicomekl floodplain is designated agricultural and held in the Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR).

blocks.text: Serpentine Sub-Area: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Subdividing ALR land requires Agricultural Land Commission permission outside limited regulation exceptions, so a large parcel is not automatically a multi-lot parcel.

Where a Surrey lot does allow a suite, only one secondary suite is permitted per dwelling unit, no suite is permitted inside a coach house or garden suite, and the suite's habitable floor area may not exceed 40 percent of the principal dwelling unit.

blocks.text: Serpentine Sub-Area: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The Serpentine and Nicomekl sea dams exist for farming, not just flood control: Surrey states they keep saline water from moving upstream where it could harm agricultural irrigation.

Servicing varies parcel by parcel on farm ground: city water, wells, and ditch or irrigation water all appear in this area, and no single servicing answer covers the sub-area — verify the specific parcel.
A registered secondary suite adds its own utility bill in Surrey: the 2026 flat rate for a suite is $454.00 for water plus $821.71 for sewer, on top of the single-family rate.
Board and feed figures for this label do not reconcile, so no Serpentine median, pace or supply figure should be quoted from either source.

blocks.text: Serpentine Sub-Area: development and new projects

items.t: South Campbell Heights Plan, around 16 Avenue and 192 Street, City of Surrey: about 249 hectares balancing regionally significant employment lands with protection of the Little Campbell River corridor. Status: plan approved by Council on December 16, 2024; the southern expansion adds about 141.5 hectares of employment land south of the existing Campbell Heights Business Park (as of November 3, 2026).

Campbell Heights road improvements, City of Surrey: widening and intersection work on 192 Street, 16 Avenue, 24 Avenue, 28 Avenue and 32 Avenue. Status: Phase 1 (192 Street, 16 Avenue to 28 Avenue) construction anticipated from summer 2025, with further phases in 2026–2027 (as of November 3, 2026).
Surrey's 2026 municipal tax rate for Residential (Class 1) is 1.84251 per $1,000 of assessed value, and the Capital Parcel Tax collected with property taxes is $300.00 for Classes 1, 8 and 9 (Farm).
The 2026 annual flat-rate utility total for a single-family dwelling is $2,856 — $1,195 water plus $1,661 sewer — and metered water and sewer bills are mailed every four months.
Waste collection is charged on the property tax notice: the 2026 single-family garbage, recycling and organics rate is $344.08 for the calendar year, due July 2.
Surrey is a listed taxable area for the provincial Speculation and Vacancy Tax, so an owner here places the annual declaration unless an exemption applies.

Highway 15 (176 Street) is the sub-area's main north–south provincial route, running through the farm ground toward the border; the City's watershed mapping shows Highway 15, Highway 99 and Highway 17 framing this lowland.
16 Avenue is the east–west road the Campbell Heights work is built around, with planned improvements at 192 Street and along 24, 28 and 32 Avenues.

blocks.text: Serpentine Sub-Area: risks and due diligence

items.t: Flood is the first check: Surrey's own floodplain reporting attributes Serpentine, Nicomekl and Little Campbell lowland flooding to local winter rainstorms, and most of that floodplain is agricultural and in the ALR.
Check ALR status parcel by parcel on Agricultural Land Commission mapping before assuming any house size, suite or subdivision right; a listing description is not an ALR determination.
Check the title at the Land Title and Survey Authority of British Columbia (LTSA) for flood covenants, dyke rights of way and building schemes, which can restrict a parcel beyond zoning.

blocks.text: What is not confirmed about Serpentine Sub-Area

items.t: The street-level boundary of the Fraser Valley board's Serpentine sub-area: no public board boundary exists, and the City of Surrey has no Serpentine planning name or boundary.

blocks.text: Surrey’s equestrian country and rural heart is Serpentine. It’s acreages and horse properties, yet King George Boulevard, Highway 99, South Surrey amenities and the U.S. border are all close.

faq.q: Is Serpentine a real Surrey neighbourhood?
faq.a: No, not in city planning terms. Serpentine is a Fraser Valley board sub-area name inside the board's Cloverdale community, alongside Clayton and Cloverdale. The City of Surrey has no Serpentine boundary, community plan or neighbourhood profile, so any street-level boundary a seller describes is a board label, not a municipal line, and should be checked against the actual parcel.

faq.q: Can I build a second house on a Serpentine acreage?
faq.a: Only within the ALC frame if the parcel is in the Agricultural Land Reserve. That frame allows one principal residence up to 500 square metres with any suite inside it, plus at most one additional residence of 90 square metres, or 186 square metres on parcels over 40 hectares.
The lowland is floodplain by design and by history. Check the individual parcel's flood and dyke status before offering.
Schools confirmed for this part of south Surrey include Morgan Elementary at 3366 156A Street and Earl Marriott Secondary at 15751 16 Avenue.

A Fraser Valley board / Paragon sub-area name — one of the three sub-areas of the board's Cloverdale community (Clayton, Cloverdale, Serpentine) — but not a City of Surrey planning or community name, so there is no City boundary or neighbourhood profile for it; listings under this label are Surrey acreage, farm and land listings on the city's southern lowland (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: What are the market figures for the wider community this sub-area sits in?
faq.a: The Cloverdale board community recorded, for September 2026: Detached 201 active listings, 32 solds, a $1,212,500 median and 19 days on market; Condos & Townhomes 194 listings, 37 solds, a $740,000 median and 32 days — community figures expressly not Serpentine's own, with Clayton the fastest-moving sub-area that month (29% detached, 21% attached) (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: What rules govern the acreage parcels on this page's feed?
faq.a: Parcel by parcel: if a parcel is in the Agricultural Land Reserve, the ALC frame applies — a principal residence capped at 500 m² with any suite inside it, at most one additional residence of 90 m² (parcels ≤40 ha) or 186 m² (>40 ha), and ALC permission required to subdivide outside limited exceptions; urban Surrey suite, coach-house and SSMUH rules apply only to non-ALR urban lots.
